summary: Deprecated model variant prorated charge appearing on finalized invoice after canary rollback
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightLens reports a finalized invoice that includes a prorated charge for a deprecated model variant (rlm-1.3-quant-depr) after they rolled back a canary deployment earlier in the billing cycle. Impact: Unexpected charge on finalized invoice amounting to $1,120. Customer reports the charge corresponds to a small percentage of inference traffic that was routed to the deprecated variant during the rollback window. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west, reserved commit in place. Expected: When a model variant is marked deprecated and traffic is rolled back to previous pinned variant, there should be no prorated charges for deprecated variants once traffic is drained or rollback completes. Actual: Finalized invoice shows a prorated line for rlm-1.3-quant-depr with non-zero quantity and a reserved-rate applied instead of hosted-fallback rate. This appears linked to a short canary rollback where routing briefly split across variants.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy canary variant rlm-1.3-quant-depr to 10% on dedicated pool us-west during billing window.
2) Detect quality regression and trigger rollback to rlm-1.3-quant-stable at T+45 minutes.
3) Observe routing logs showing a small fraction of requests still hitting the deprecated variant during the rollback window (approx 0.8% over 30 minutes).
4) Allow billing cycle to finalize.
5) Observe invoice line for rlm-1.3-quant-depr showing prorated reserved-hours and positive charge.
logs:
Invoice excerpt: 
- Line 345: rlm-1.3-quant-depr | Reserved variant prorated hours | qty: 3.2 | rate_id: reserved-hybrid-usw | amount: $1,120.00
Routing trace snippet (2026-03-02T14:42:10Z - 2026-03-02T15:12:05Z):
- request-ids: [redacted] routed to rlm-1.3-quant-depr at 0.6-1.2% of total.
Postback delivery log: postback-id 8f7a: success -> reconciler accepted -> billed under reserved-hybrid-usw
Note: Postbacks for the same window include entries tagged with deprecated_variant=true and tag migration_policy=canary-rollback.
investigation_notes: Support verified invoice line and correlated timestamps with customer's rollback window.
Billing team confirms postback reconciler accepted variant tag 'rlm-1.3-quant-depr' and applied reserved rate because reconciler matched variant to customer's dedicated commit id.

Serving/runtime team found brief KV-cache TTL mismatch: router continued to route a small percentage to deprecated pod replicas for ~27 minutes after rollback due to stale prefix cache on 2 edge nodes.
Rollback was executed correctly at control plane level, but edge drain handshake failed for a subset of connections causing late routed traffic that still generated postbacks.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: race between route update + prefix cache invalidation and postback attribution logic which maps variant->rate at ingestion time. Late postbacks were not re-attributed when variant was marked deprecated.
Customer provided request IDs and export of their traffic which matched postback records; we validated 98% of those postbacks correlate to the timeframe in question.
No evidence of duplicate postbacks or retries that would inflate quantity; charge matches legitimately routed requests.

Billing policy note: When a variant receives traffic during a customer's reserved commit window and reconciler maps to that commit id, reserved rates apply even if variant is deprecated later in cycle. This policy needs clarification for canary rollbacks.

Related config: reconciler uses first-seen variant tag to pick rate unless a reclassification job marks it differently. Reclassification job runs daily and did not reclassify these postbacks because the finalization occurred before cron job ran.

Potential mitigations: (a) fast reclassification on rollback events, (b) ensure prefix cache invalidation propagates synchronously for rollback operations, (c) treat deprecated variants with special billing attribution rules during rollbacks.
Estimate impact: single customer $1.12k charge; could affect other customers who performed similar rapid rollback within billing window but magnitude expected low.
